claims.text: The starting material is a W–Cu composite containing W particles or interconnected W ligaments in a Cu matrix.
A 1–5 nm Ta film is deposited on W surfaces by atomic layer deposition before consolidation.
The proposed consolidation and sintering temperature is approximately 1200°C.
The Ta coating will form a continuous ultrathin interlayer at W/Cu interfaces.
The Ta interlayer will act as a diffusion barrier at W/Cu interfaces.
The Ta barrier will suppress thermally activated W–Cu interdiffusion during consolidation.
The Ta barrier will suppress thermally activated W–Cu interdiffusion during service exposure up to approximately 400°C.
Suppressing interdiffusion will prevent or reduce phase separation.
The Ta interlayer will reduce interfacial void nucleation and void formation.
Reducing phase separation and void formation will preserve a coherent and mechanically robust W/Cu interface.
A coherent interface with fewer voids will improve thermal connectivity.
Ta-coated composites will have a more homogeneous interfacial microstructure than untreated composites.
Ta-coated composites will have a lower interfacial void fraction than untreated composites.
Ta-coated composites will exhibit higher thermal conductivity than untreated composites under heat-transfer conditions.
Ta-coated composites will exhibit higher thermal conductivity than untreated composites after or under irradiation-relevant conditions.
Untreated W–Cu composites typically exhibit phase separation under high-temperature and irradiation conditions.
Untreated W–Cu composites typically develop interfacial voids under high-temperature and irradiation conditions.
The claimed service boundary is irradiation and heat-transfer exposure at temperatures up to approximately 400°C.
